title: Exponential of Gaussian coordinate magnitudes is integrable
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $c\in\mathbb R$, and let $p\in[0,\infty]$ be finite. On $\mathbb R^n$ with product standard Gaussian measure, the function $x\mapsto \exp\!\left(c\sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|\right)$ belongs to $L^p$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a nonnegative extended real exponent and $p\ne\infty$
